clue.text: Very basic accommodation a draw: however, be careful buying it!

blocks.note: a cave is about the most primitive shelter there is
taken as written
to draw someone in is to tempt them
loosely, 'or' and 'however' both introduce an alternative or qualification

explanation.surface: A sales pitch for a spartan holiday cave, with a raffle thrown in and a warning to shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: Caveat emptor is the Latin legal maxim 'let the buyer beware'. The equation of 'however' with OR is a loose one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin maxim warns a purchaser that the risk of a bad bargain lies with them, so they must take care.

clue.text: Conducting search, billions invested in future

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for billion
the coming days are the future ones

explanation.surface: A financial forecaster scouring the markets while billions are poured into futures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Future' is an adjective here, as in 'the coming year'; the financial picture of futures trading is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, so combing is carrying out a painstaking search.

clue.text: Shortage of animal produce in vehicle — one wouldn't want it!

indicators.note: a shortage means something falls short, so the word loses its final letter
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a van is a road vehicle
an egg is food produced by an animal

explanation.surface: A delivery van running short of eggs and meat, though one customer would not care.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: 'it' is the animal produce, which a vegan refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan avoids all food from animals, so such a person would decline eggs and similar produce.

clue.text: Sign of joiner sprinkling Parmesan over top of dish

indicators.note: sprinkled cheese is scattered about, so its letters land in a new order
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

blocks.note: the cheese name rearranged
the initial letter of dish

explanation.surface: A carpenter showing his taste by grating Parmesan over a plated dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter, but here it is the word 'and', which joins things; in a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The & symbol stands for 'and', the most common connecting word, so it is the sign of a joiner.

clue.text: Archer hurt, shooting vertically?

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a word upward makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: something that hurts is sore

explanation.surface: An archer wounded while firing arrows straight up into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Eros, the Greek god of love, is the archer whose arrows make people fall in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros, like Roman Cupid, is pictured with bow and arrows, making him the mythological archer.

clue.text: Hold up a short novel, for example — that might amuse baby

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom upward
a short version of a word is cut off before its last letter

blocks.note: to hold is to keep
taken as written
a novel is one kind of book

explanation.surface: Someone delaying a brief novel, apparently written to entertain an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' reads as 'delay', but splits into a verb and a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Peekaboo is the game of hiding then revealing one's face, a classic way to make an infant laugh.

clue.text: Love which exists in peaceful place

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O
'as' can stand for 'which', as in 'the same as I said'
something that exists is

explanation.surface: A romantic thought: love lives on in a tranquil spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an oasis is a calm refuge amid turmoil, from the fertile spot in a desert.

clue.text: New prince eating old, old cheese

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside
a new version is remade, so the letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
again O for old

explanation.surface: A young royal tucking into a very old cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Pecorino is a hard Italian cheese made from ewe's milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecorino is a named variety, so it is a specific example of a cheese.

clue.text: Observe cricket side, perfect

blocks.note: to spot is to notice or observe
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket fan watching a team and pronouncing it flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (or leg) side of the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is informal British praise for something exactly right, hence flawless.

clue.text: Hole behind me perfect for amplifier

indicators.note: something behind another follows it, so the hole is placed after the word it is behind

blocks.note: taken as written
a gap is a hole or opening
to hone something is to refine or perfect it

explanation.surface: A gap behind the speaker that suits a sound system nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind me' places the hole after ME; 'perfect' is a verb, not praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone is a cone that makes a voice louder, a simple sound-boosting device.

clue.text: Dear Sir, this editorial's extraordinarily pretentious, first of all

indicators.note: the first of all these words means taking each one's opening letter

blocks.note: initial letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A reader's letter to the editor complaining of pompous leader writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear Sir' looks like a letter's greeting, but 'Dear' stands apart as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep price is an expensive one, so dear and steep both mean costly.

clue.text: Goner undone by one cut

indicators.note: something undone is taken apart, so its letters can be put back differently

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the word goner rearranged

explanation.surface: A doomed man brought down by a single blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means beside, so the numeral sits next to the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them deliberately, refusing to acknowledge them.

clue.text: Document graduate left

blocks.note: to graduate is to pass a course
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A certificate showing a graduate has gone away.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is an official paper proving identity and nationality for travel.

clue.text: All six blokes initially entertained by funny, garrulous type

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word
guests entertained by a host are taken in, held inside

blocks.note: a funny, as a noun, is a joke or gag
first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Six men are amused by a comic chatterbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' is a noun here, a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is an informal word for someone who talks too much, a talkative windbag.

clue.text: Two saw a drunk heading for yacht — one hiding on it

indicators.note: drunk words stagger about, so their letters are mixed up
a heading is the top, so the word's first letter is taken

blocks.note: the three words rearranged
initial of yacht

explanation.surface: A pair spot a tipsy person making for a yacht, someone concealed aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to the yacht, so the definition reads off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway hides aboard a vessel to travel without paying, exactly someone hidden on a yacht.

clue.text: Arrest prophet from the East — East African

indicators.note: across clues read from west to east, so coming from the east means right to left

blocks.note: to nail a criminal is to catch and arrest them
Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: Police detain a holy man arriving from the Orient, an African.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia lies in the Horn of Africa, so a Somalian is a native of an eastern African country.

clue.text: Great leader bitter, cross with Queen

blocks.note: bitter is a British style of beer, an ale
X is the cross shape
with means and, joining things
ER is the royal cypher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A famous commander feeling resentful and angry with his monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' and 'cross' seem to describe the leader's mood, but bitter is a type of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great, king of Macedon, was a conqueror whose title includes the word in the clue.

clue.text: This woman's scary, inferring pa is less organised?

definitions.text: This woman's scary, inferring pa is less organised?

blocks.note: surface reading: a frightening woman, the type who devours lovers
setter's reading: whoever eats a man leaves father with fewer organs, less organ-ised

explanation.surface: A daunting woman whose arrival suggests Dad's life is falling into disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' splits as organ-ised: a literal devourer of men would leave pa short of organs.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound names a predatory woman who uses and discards male partners, and literally a creature that devours people.

clue.text: General method acting seen on this US street

definitions.text: acting seen on this US street

blocks.note: broad means general, as in a broad outline
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: Method acting in general can be seen on a famous New York avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Method acting' is a decoy phrase: method and acting belong to different parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway in New York is synonymous with the city's main theatre district, where stage acting is seen.

clue.text: Break clasp

blocks.note: first meaning: to give way or collapse under pressure
second meaning: a fastener on a belt or shoe

explanation.surface: A fastening snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal fastener on a belt, and the verb for crumpling or giving way under strain.

clue.text: Compensate for trigger

blocks.note: first meaning: to counterbalance one thing against another
second meaning: to cause something to start, like an alarm

explanation.surface: Making amends for having started something off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to offset a cost or loss and to cause an alarm or explosion to start.

clue.text: Rogue player

blocks.note: first meaning: a cheat who fiddles accounts or swindles
second meaning: a violinist, one who plays the fiddle

explanation.surface: A sportsman who has gone off the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddle means both to swindle and the violin, so the noun covers a con artist and a violinist.

clue.text: Bosses cut machinery out

indicators.note: a cut word is trimmed, losing its final letter
letters put out of order are rearranged

blocks.note: the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: Managers switching off the factory equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairmen head boards and companies, so they are the people in charge.

clue.text: Quickly produce series at a higher level

blocks.note: a run is a series, as a winning run
up means higher

explanation.surface: Making a television series fast so it can move to a bigger stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up clothes or a bill is to make or produce them hastily.

clue.text: Destroyed — as are double-barrelled names?

blocks.note: first meaning: ruined
second meaning: names like Smith-Jones contain a hyphen, a short dash

explanation.walkthrough: 'Double-barrelled' suggests a shotgun, which fits 'Destroyed', but it means hyphenated surnames.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes that are ruined are crushed, and a hyphenated surname is joined by a dash mark.

clue.text: Nothing in this designed for lift

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it
designed letters are arranged to a fresh plan

blocks.note: taken as written
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing here was designed to raise anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a device for raising heavy loads, and to hoist is to raise.

clue.text: Deposit saved by couple, essential

indicators.note: what is saved is kept inside, held within the following words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A pair saving a down payment, which is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the sediment that settles at the bottom of a wine cask or bottle.

clue.text: King literarily requiring new master

blocks.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A king in a book needs a fresh tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to learn it thoroughly; as verbs they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Winger's notes about badly made exercise machine

indicators.note: badly done means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a bird is a winger, and its warbling notes are a trill
the word made rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer's notes on a poorly built gym machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer, but it is a bird, something with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a moving belt on which a person walks or runs for exercise.

clue.text: Reports with wit unusually penned by senior journalist

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so letters get reordered
something penned is enclosed, as in a pen

blocks.note: Sr is the abbreviation for senior
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran newspaperman writing quirky, amusing reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportswriter is a journalist who covers sport, one type of newspaper writer.
